claims.text: The rider's own chat message asked the driver to stop at Paya Lebar Square, and the driver's GPS trace corroborates the detour: the vehicle passed within 35.99 m of the waypoint_hint coordinate carried on that message, well inside the 200 m corroboration threshold. The instruction came from the rider (MSG-02812-001), was sent at 10:19:39, before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and names a specific place. Under POL-RD-04 the excess distance attributable to this rider-requested stop is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

The rider's instruction is not vague: it names 'Paya Lebar Square' and the platform resolved that text to a waypoint_hint coordinate at ingest (lat 1.381532, lng 103.831811). The driver's reply 'ok' at 10:19:59 confirms acceptance. This is exactly the 'stop at Jurong Point first' form POL-RD-04(a)-(c) contemplates, so the clause is available and the corroboration test can be run on the record.

The rider's claim that this was 'a tour' rather than a requested stop is contradicted by the rider's own message. The rider asked for the stop; the driver complied; the extra distance is the rider's own doing. Under POL-RD-04 the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded, and the driver is not penalised for a detour the rider requested.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes: 107 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s. POL-RD-07(a)-(c) is not engaged, so the trace is not impaired and the deviation measurement stands on the trace as recorded. The rider cannot escape the rider-requested-detour finding by attacking the trace's integrity.

The rider's profile shows zero deviation claims in the last 60 days and zero substantiated, and zero disputes with this counterparty in 90 days. Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and has not been shown to be a serial claimant; but equally, the rider's own chat message defeats the claim on its merits, and the burden-shifting test does not rescue a claim the rider's own words contradict.

The driver's profile shows zero deviation flags in the last 90 days across 368 completed trips, and zero disputes with this counterparty in 90 days. Under POL-RD-06 no repeat-deviation pattern is established, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral is warranted. The driver's record on this trip is clean and the detour was rider-caused.

The fare breakdown shows no ERP gantries charged and no airport surcharge, so there is no pass-through line to correct under POL-RD-09. The rider was billed for 13.5 km against a trace of 13.52 km, a shortfall of 0.02 km, far below the 1.0 km threshold for driver compensation under POL-RD-04. No billing-integrity defect exists on this record.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload. No party has cited it as an exculpatory record, and the driver does not rely on a traffic cause. Under POL-RD-13 the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction, and it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The case is decided on the rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04.

The rider's claim of 13.52 km against 10.4 km optimal is arithmetically correct on the trace, but the excess is entirely attributable to the rider-requested stop at Paya Lebar Square. Under POL-RD-04 the excess is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, so no deviation survives and the outcome is NO_ACTION: the charge stands as billed.

ruling.explanation:
To both of you: the trip ran 13.52 km against a platform optimal of 10.4 km — an excess of 3.12 km, or 30% — and that passes the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km). But the excess is entirely explained by the stop the rider asked for, so there is no deviation left to refund and the charge of SGD 19.69 stands. The ruling is NO_ACTION and the SGD 4.00 of disputed fare is not returned.

Rider: your own chat message at 10:19:39 — 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something' — is a rider instruction naming a specific place, sent before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and the driver accepted it at 10:19:59. The GPS trace shows the vehicle passing within 36 m of the waypoint the platform resolved from your message (Paya Lebar Square), well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration threshold. POL-RD-04 excludes the distance of a rider-requested detour before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, and with the detour removed the remaining excess is nil, so no refund is due. Your characterisation that you 'only asked for a quick stop, not a tour' does not change the clause's test: the place you named is the reason for the extra distance and the driver drove to it. For transparency, had the detour not been rider-requested the POL-RD-02 recomputation would have been charged_total 19.69 less recomputed_fare 16.32, a refund of SGD 3.40; that computation does not run here because POL-RD-04 removes the excess. POL-RD-11 does not apply — the fare is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE.

Driver: your arithmetic and the rider-advocate's are right. An excess of 3.12 km / 30% is above the 20% / 0.8 km gate but below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality line, so the POL-RD-06 uplift and conduct referral are not triggered. Your profile is clean on the only counters POL-RD-06 permits — deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 368 — so no repeat-deviation pattern is established; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and has not been used. No driver compensation is due: the ledger bills 13.5 km against a trace of 13.52 km, a shortfall of 0.02 km, below the 1.0 km threshold in POL-RD-04. No ERP gantries and no airport surcharge were charged, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct.

On the evidence: the GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 107 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so the deviation measurement and its removal both rest on a clean trace. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); neither side asserted an external traffic cause, so under POL-RD-13 its absence is a gap in the bundle and not a contradiction, and it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5). Two claims that cited that artifact without disclosing its impairment were discarded by the referee.

Confidence is 0.90. The deciding fact — that the Paya Lebar Square stop was requested by the rider — is carried by the chat log (EV-CHAT-02812, weight 1.0) and independently by the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02812, weight 1.0), so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the platform-wide floor of 0.70 is met. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. The monetary effect is nil, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation: To the rider and the driver: I have reviewed trip TRP-02812 (Serangoon to Blk 130 Bukit Batok West Ave 6). The ruling is NO_ACTION — the charge stands as billed and no money moves. The distance is confirmed on the trace. POL-RD-01 measures actual distance from the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy, so the governing figure is 13.52 km (EV-GPS-02812) against a booked optimal of 10.4 km (EV-TRIP-02812): an excess of 3.12 km, or 30%. Both establishment tests are met (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is established. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (under 50% and under 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile uplift and any conduct referral are not engaged. The whole excess is nevertheless exonerated under POL-RD-04 because the rider asked for it. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02812) records the rider's own message MSG-02812-001 at 10:19:39 — 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something' — sent by the rider, 60 seconds after the meter started and before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and naming a specific place. The platform resolved that text to a waypoint at Paya Lebar Square (1.381532, 103.831811), and the driver replied 'ok' at 10:19:59. The GPS trace corroborates the request: the vehicle passed within 35.99 m of that waypoint at 10:27:39, inside the 200 m threshold POL-RD-04 sets, and the size of the detour (3.12 km off a Serangoon–Bukit Batok run) matches the stop. POL-RD-04 excludes the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor, so no deviation survives and nothing remains to refund. I do not accept the rider's description of this as 'a tour': the chat log and the trace show one requested stop and no extra distance beyond it. They are consistent with each other, so no POL-RD-10(7) contradiction arises and there is nothing to escalate. No driver compensation is due: the fare ledger (EV-FARE-02812) billed 13.5 km against a trace of 13.52 km — a shortfall of 0.02 km, far below the 1.0 km threshold in POL-RD-04. POL-RD-09 gives nothing to correct: the fare carries no ERP gantry lines, no airport surcharge and no unmatched charge line. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. The driver's profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 368), so no POL-RD-06(c) referral is produced, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field that clause asks for. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). No party asserts a traffic cause, and a missing advisory that no one has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) escalation (POL-RD-13); no fact rests on it, so it does not reduce confidence. Two claims that cited that artifact without naming its issue code were discarded by the referee and are listed in the audit record. Confidence is 0.95: the ruling rests on the chat log and the GPS trace, both at weight 1.0 and independent of each other, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The monetary effect is zero, below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, and no clause produces a referral.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, you largely agree on the facts and the record supports that agreement. The disputed SGD 4.00 is not refunded; the fare of SGD 19.69 stands as charged (EV-FARE-02812, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

Route and exoneration. The trip ran Serangoon to Bukit Batok (TRP-02812). At 10:19:39, one minute after the meter started (10:18:39), the rider wrote 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something' (EV-CHAT-02812, MSG-02812-001) and the driver answered 'ok' at 10:19:59. The platform resolved that text to a waypoint_hint (1.381532, 103.831811), and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02812) puts the car within 36 m of it at 10:27:39. POL-RD-04 is therefore satisfied in full: the instruction came from the rider, was given before the car left the direct route, names a specific place, and is corroborated inside the 200 m test. The excess it produced is excluded before the deviation test, so no deviation survives and no refund runs. The rider's own filing concedes the stop was requested; the 'tour' characterisation is not supported by any evidence — the driver's statement and the rider's message agree, and the trace shows the car going to the waypoint the rider named.

Measurements relied on. Actual distance is 13.52 km from the GPS trace, the governing field under POL-RD-01 (the trip record's 13.5 km is a rounded copy and was not used); the optimal was 10.4 km, so the measured excess was 3.12 km / 30%, which is exactly the Paya Lebar detour and back. The trace is clean for policy purposes: 107 fixes at 10 s spacing, 100% coverage, zero gaps, so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and no corroboration question arises.

Materiality and pattern. The excess is not MATERIAL (30% is under 50% and 3.12 km is under 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered; in any event deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 368 completed trips, so no pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c). The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags raised in argument is context-only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used.

Billing. The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-02812), so POL-RD-11 does not apply, but no distance or time refund arises because the excess is exonerated. There are no ERP gantry lines and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09 yields no correction and no billing-integrity referral. Billed distance 13.5 km against the 13.52 km trace is a 0.02 km shortfall, far below the 1.0 km threshold for driver compensation under POL-RD-04, so none is awarded.

Missing advisory. EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). No party asserts a traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is not invoked and, under POL-RD-13, its absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction; it triggers no escalation, carries no fact, and does not enter the confidence cap.

Confidence and execution. All artifacts carrying the deciding facts (EV-CHAT-02812, EV-GPS-02812, EV-TRIP-02812) are at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect is nil, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, and no clause produces a referral. The charge stands and the file is closed; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

To both parties — this ruling was made without a human reviewer, and either party may appeal it once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04).
